subject: Request: SIG & subprocessor residency details for PulseHealth RFP
messages:
From: Carmen Lopez <carmen.lopez@pulsehealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: AuditEdge <audit@auditedge.com>, procurement@pulsehealth.com
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Request: SIG/CAIQ + subprocessor residency & transient access details for RFP

Hi Vanessa —

We're working through a short RFP for our inference platform evaluation. As part of our security gating we need the following artifacts and clarifications by EOD next Friday (2026-08-27):

- Completed SIG/CAIQ (or SOC2 mapping) artifacts you can share with an external auditor.
- A current subprocessor roster (CSV) that includes geographic residency (country of processing), data types processed, and whether KMS keys are customer- or provider-managed.
- Clarification on transient/ephemeral access models used by your runtime (token lifetime, who has admin access to KV cache/KMS paths, and any third parties that receive ephemeral credentials).
- A simple attestation that nothing in the roster includes onshore/offshore exceptions that would conflict with our EU residency requirements for a scoped workflow.

Our external auditor (cc'd) may ask for a short call or to validate a couple of items directly; please include a point of contact and an access window for secure artifact transfer.

Can you confirm receipt and an internal owner we can expect to see these from?

Thanks,
Carmen Lopez
Head of Vendor Risk — PulseHealth

--
PulseHealth | pulsehealth.com
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: SIG/CAIQ + subprocessor residency & transient access details for RFP

Thanks Carmen — received. Internal owners below and proposed split:

- Marissa: pull the latest SIG/CAIQ pack and a SOC2 crosswalk; sanitize and export as PDF (redwood_SIG3_responses_2026.pdf).
- Rachel: compile KMS/residency map and note customer-managed KMS options (kms_residency_map_2026.xlsx).
- Karthik: produce a short write-up on transient/ephemeral access (token TTLs, who/what gets ephemeral creds, audit trails) and export subprocessor roster with residency columns (subprocessor_roster_2026-08.csv).

Timeline: we can get draft artifacts to Carmen and AuditEdge by EOD Friday (08/22 PDT) if everyone moves fast. If the auditor wants an online review we'll schedule a 30-min slot on Mon/Tue next week.

Marissa — please confirm you can generate the SIG/CAIQ export and indicate any items that will need redaction (customer examples, sample logs). Rachel/Karthik — confirm availability to complete your pieces.

I'll coordinate the secure sharing link and handle the attestation language once drafts are in.

-Vanessa

On Thu, Aug 20, 2026 at 10:05 AM Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks Carmen — received. Internal owners below and proposed split:

Attached draft artifacts and notes (stubs below). I'm keeping PII/sample log lines redacted. Key callouts:

1) SIG/CAIQ pack (redwood_SIG3_responses_2026.pdf) — Completed. We used SIG-Lite mapping for the RFP; where full evidence is sensitive I've added an evidence locator (internal doc ID) and a short justification. Note: policy references to ephemeral key rotation dates are high level; Rachel to add the residency specifics.

2) Subprocessor roster (subprocessor_roster_2026-08.csv) — Included columns: subprocessor_name, service_purpose, country_of_processing, category (infra/telemetry/analytics), access_type (service_account/admin/ephemeral). I flagged two runtime infra partners that have EU processing footprints and one onshore-only telemetry partner.

3) KMS residency map (kms_residency_map_2026.xlsx) — Rachel, please complete the KMS owner column (provider vs. customer).

Attachments (for PulseHealth review):
- redwood_SIG3_responses_2026.pdf (redacted where necessary)
- subprocessor_roster_2026-08.csv (PII-free roster)
- kms_residency_map_2026.xlsx (workbook; sheet 1 = residency, sheet 2 = key access model)

Next steps: once Rachel and Karthik confirm items, Vanessa can push the secure link to PulseHealth. I'm comfortable with a brief attestation phrasing along the lines of: "To the best of Redwood Inference's knowledge as of 2026-08-22, the attached roster accurately represents our engaged subprocessors and their primary processing residency; no undisclosed offshore processing exists for the scoped workflow." Let me know if legal wants different language.

-Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Request: SIG/CAIQ + subprocessor residency & transient access details for RFP

Hi Carmen — thanks for the request and for the patience while we pulled materials together. Attached are the artifacts and a short summary for your auditor.

What we shared (secure link sent to Carmen and AuditEdge):
- redwood_SIG3_responses_2026.pdf — SIG-Lite export with evidence locators for sensitive items.
- subprocessor_roster_2026-08.csv — current roster with country_of_processing and access_type columns.
- kms_residency_map_2026.xlsx — outlines which services use provider-managed KMS vs. customer-managed keys and the residency for key material.

Short answers to your questions:
- Transient/ephemeral access: runtime issues ephemeral credentials for autoscaling workers (short-lived tokens TTL = 15m by default). Admin access to KV caches and KMS key rotation is limited to our core infra ops group (on a least-privilege, auditable role). No third party receives long-lived admin credentials; partners receive scoped, time-limited service tokens where required for integration.
- Attestation: per Marissa's suggested wording — we confirm the roster reflects our subprocessors and their primary processing residency for the scoped workflow as of the attached export.

If AuditEdge wants to validate anything directly we can open a short window next week for a secured review (please propose two 30-min slots). Also copying HubSpot record for this account (HSP-98721).

Secure download link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExampleSecureLink (access restricted; link shared with Carmen and audit@auditedge.com)

If you need the SOC2 crosswalk instead of SIG-Lite, say the word and we will produce it within 48 hours.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Head of Strategic Accounts, Redwood Inference
vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0147
